name: The Loft
label: Creation Records
lede: Alan McGee heard 'Why Does the Rain' at his own club and wanted it as a single. Two Creation releases later the Loft broke up mid-set at the Hammersmith Palais, and it took them forty years to make an album.

eras.title: A band called the Living Room
eras.text: Two Polytechnic students in Leyton found a singer in an Islington pub and a drummer who knew Alan McGee. McGee's new club then took their name, so they took the room upstairs.

years.src: WriteWyattUK: Room at the top · Pete Astor: The Loft
years.h: Andy Strickland and Bill Prince find a singer at the Pied Bull
years.p: The two met at the Polytechnic of Central London and shared a house in Leyton. They recruited [[Pete Astor|e9cb7de9-0508-4e3a-b370-bb23c4b1578d]] after seeing his band News of Birds at the Pied Bull in Islington.
years.xp:
Astor's version: they came up to him after the gig "and asked if I might want to be the singer in their band." He said no at first, then agreed to play at their drummer Andy's rehearsal room in Tufnell Park, and they met every Sunday afternoon. By the end of the year they were calling themselves the Living Room.

Dave Morgan, who already knew Alan McGee from the Communication Club scene, took over the drums later. The touchstones were [[Lou Reed|9d1ebcfe-4c15-4d18-95d3-d919898638a1]], [[Television|490bde43-5edb-4a93-b3b3-7a0465fd8909]], The Only Ones and The Modern Lovers.

years.src: WriteWyattUK: Down from The Loft · Pete Astor: The Loft · Backseat Mafia · Wikipedia: The Loft
years.h: "I wanna do a single of that!" says the man on the door
years.p: Alan McGee opens his club, the Living Room, at the Adams Arms. When he hears the band play 'Why Does the Rain', he wants to put it out.
years.xp:
Astor had spotted a news item about a new club opening in the upstairs room of the Adams Arms. They became regulars, got to know McGee and Dick Green, and were offered a support slot with [[Television Personalities|62c2cd94-30a8-43ed-9d06-8f689111c69c]]. Astor: "one of the few places in London where we felt at home."

He had already played his songs to [[Rough Trade|4f4b0013-1704-4936-a769-e6e8a6e08ff8]]'s Geoff Travis, who told him to come back in a year. McGee, working the door, didn't need the year. The club had the band's name, so the band renamed itself the Loft.

years.h: First Living Room gig, opening for Television Personalities
years.p: Strickland remembers the Living Room as "really the only place we could get a gig." Their first night there is in support of [[Television Personalities|62c2cd94-30a8-43ed-9d06-8f689111c69c]].

eras.title: Creation's best bet walks off the stage
eras.text: The Loft were among the first bands on Creation Records, with two singles that set the label's early tone. They got radio sessions, TV and a national tour, and then fell apart in front of the audience on the tour's last night.

years.cap: Strickland, Morgan, Astor and Prince live, c. 1984
years.h: The Roebuck: the Jesus and Mary Chain on first, then the Loft
years.p: The Living Room moves to the Roebuck on Tottenham Court Road. One June bill has the Loft supporting [[Microdisney|ca8ac7f8-fc63-43a9-9761-46c253e66ac3]], with [[The Jesus and Mary Chain|e938a15c-b17e-4e7a-9f68-ff0d536cab44]] opening.
years.xp: Live recordings from the Roebuck that June turned up decades later on the 2021 compilation Ghost Trains & Country Lanes.

years.src: Discogs: Alive in the Living Room
years.h: 'Your Door Shines Like Gold' on Creation's first LP
years.p: Alive in the Living Room, CRE LP 001, is recorded live at McGee's club between August 1983 and February 1984. The Loft close side one.
years.xp: The bill also has the [[Jasmine Minks|c3552faf-9c1c-46ba-af13-653fe2fdcf9c]], [[The Pastels|9d6108ad-dbc2-4bf1-a746-edc1044d2749]], [[The Mekons|66d2169c-dea5-46d3-b4cb-52ed87b24ab0]] and Television Personalities, whose closing track is cut short by a police raid on the club.

years.src: Discogs: Why Does the Rain · Backseat Mafia · The Line of Best Fit
years.h: 'Why Does the Rain' is Creation single CRE 009
years.p: [[Joe Foster|6a850a84-6293-4788-9e05-ccd9fd4f0315]] and the band produce it, with 'Like' on the B-side. It's the song McGee heard at the Living Room door.
years.xp:
There was never a contract. Astor: "there was always only a handshake deal which remained in place until Alan sold the label to Sony."

The Line of Best Fit later called it one of the label's first true classics. Astor kept the song: [[The Weather Prophets|8bd0e8b7-081a-4b32-b855-b38134074b35]] re-recorded it for Mayflower in 1987.

years.h: A Radio 1 session for Janice Long
years.p: The Loft record a session for Janice Long's evening show on BBC Radio 1.

years.src: Discogs: Up the Hill · WriteWyattUK: Room at the top
yt: Up the Hill and Down the Slope, 1985
years.h: Leamington Spa, two days, and a Richard Hell cover
years.p: Cut with John A. Rivers at Woodbine Studios on February 19–20, the four-track EP is CRE 015. Astor wrote three songs; the fourth is [[Richard Hell|5c04c739-afeb-43de-a7cb-0991f625e1f6]]'s 'Time'.
years.xp:
[[Robert Forster|c790898c-8e86-470c-88de-3d2c7560db10]] of [[The Go-Betweens|2fb4db11-8349-47ab-b1a6-f04f011699ff]] complimented the band's guitar work on 'Time'.

The band played the title track on BBC2's The Oxford Road Show.
play: Up the Hill and Down the Slope
Up the Hill and Down the Slope

years.h: £100 a night opening for Terry Hall's Colourfield
years.p: The Colourfield tour opens at the Cornwall Coliseum in St Austell, with the Loft as support across the country.

q: A bit of a hothead, not communicating things properly and clearly
years.src: WriteWyattUK: Down from The Loft · WriteWyattUK: Room at the top · Backseat Mafia · Northern Exposure · Discogs: The Loft
years.h: The Loft split mid-set on the tour's last night, at the Palais
years.p: They stop mid-song on the tour's last night at the Hammersmith Palais, in front of about 3,000 people.
years.xp:
Strickland put it down to bad communication; Astor said he was "a bit of a hothead, not communicating things properly and clearly," and that the clash was mostly between him and Strickland. Asked in 2020 whether the split was planned, he answered: "Ah, the hot bloodedness of youth!"

A live recording of the Palais show exists and has never been released.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Loft · WriteWyattUK: Room at the top
years.h: Two Weather Prophets, a Caretaker Race and the Wishing Stones
years.p: Astor and Morgan start [[The Weather Prophets|8bd0e8b7-081a-4b32-b855-b38134074b35]] on Creation. Strickland goes on to form The Caretaker Race in 1986 and Prince The Wishing Stones.
years.xp: Strickland was already writing for Record Mirror, where he freelanced until about 1990. The Caretaker Race made Hangover Square with [[Stephen Street|47c7deb5-2e24-45ec-944e-d9d103afb312]] in 1990.

eras.title: Creation collects the singles
eras.text: Four years after the split, Creation put the Loft's handful of releases on one record.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Loft · Discogs: The Loft
years.p: Creation's compilation pulls the singles and the rest of the band's recordings onto one LP.

eras.title: Same four, forty years on
eras.text: The four original members patched things up and played again. Then, four decades after the Palais, they made their first album and a second one a year later.

years.h: Rev-Ola reissues the Loft as Magpie Eyes
years.p: The second career compilation, Magpie Eyes 1982–1985, arrives as the band starts talking again.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Loft · WriteWyattUK: Room at the top
years.h: Back together, with 'Model Village' on Static Caravan
years.p: The four re-form and put out a new single. Strickland says they had cleared the air.
years.xp: The reunion has an annual ritual: a pre-Christmas Italian meal, where they rarely talk about the Loft. "There's only ever been four of us," Strickland says. "A nice little club."

years.cap: The Loft at NYC Popfest, Cameo Gallery, Brooklyn, May 29, 2015
years.src: The Big Takeover · WriteWyattUK: Down from The Loft · Wikipedia: The Loft
yt: Up the Hill and Down the Slope, 6 Music session, 2015
years.h: First US show, thirty-five years in, at a Williamsburg gallery
years.p: The Loft play NYC Popfest at Cameo Gallery, mixing their own songs with two by [[The Weather Prophets|8bd0e8b7-081a-4b32-b855-b38134074b35]].
years.xp:
The set ran from 'Why Does the Rain' and 'Up the Hill and Down the Slope' to Richard Hell's 'Time', plus Weather Prophets songs 'Joe Shmo & the Eskimo' and 'Can't Keep My Mind Off You'.

The same year brought a London show at the Lexington, one of Astor's favourite gigs of recent years, and a BBC 6 Music session for Gideon Coe.

years.p: Ghost Trains & Country Lanes adds the reunion recordings, the 2015 6 Music session and live tapes from the Roebuck in June 1984.

years.src: Tapete Records: The Loft · Northern Exposure · Metacritic · Wikipedia: The Loft
yt: Everything Changes Everything Stays the Same, short documentary, 2025
years.h: Forty years after the Palais, a debut album
years.p: Recorded in summer 2024, Everything Changes, Everything Stays the Same comes out on Tapete Records. Tapete says it made the Top 20 of the vinyl chart.
years.xp:
Sean Read of Dexys produced it, in Hackney in August 2024. The first single, 'Dr Clarke', came out on January 9, 2025; Astor says it's about "charismatic types who get people doing things they don't want to do."

Reviews were good: 80 on Metacritic from four. Glide wondered "just how big this band could have been" without the 1985 split. Strickland: "The Loft has always been just the four of us."

q: It feels good to be in a real band again
years.h: Astor and Strickland write together on Badges
years.p: Sean Read produces the second album at Famous Times in Hackney. It's the first time Astor has co-written songs with Strickland.
